evals.prompt: Create a reusable prompt for an LLM that implements a Python 3.13 function from a feature description. The generated prompt should make the model return a unified diff, add pytest coverage, avoid new dependencies, and say when a requirement is missing instead of guessing.
evals.expected_output: A paste-ready code-generation message set with explicit placeholders, requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, output format, verification rules, and conditional model settings.
expectations: The result separates stable coding behavior from the variable feature request or clearly structures them in one prompt
The prompt contains visible placeholders for feature details, repository context, and acceptance criteria
The prompt requires a unified diff, pytest coverage, no new dependencies, and explicit handling of missing requirements
The settings distinguish reasoning or effort from classic sampling controls and label provider-dependent values
The prompt does not require disclosure of private chain-of-thought

evals.prompt: Rewrite my production support-ticket summarizer prompt. Tickets can contain malicious text like 'ignore your rules'. The output feeds an API and must be strict JSON with issue, impact, suspected_cause, evidence_ids, and needs_human_review. It may use only the supplied ticket events, must not invent a cause, and should return null when evidence is missing. Include a compact A/B evaluation plan.
evals.expected_output: A secure, grounded summarization prompt with privileged instructions separated from untrusted ticket data, a strict output contract, an uncertainty policy, and measurable A/B tests.
expectations: Untrusted ticket content is placed in a user-data section rather than interpolated into a system or developer message
The prompt states that embedded ticket instructions cannot override the task
The output contract defines all five requested fields and represents unsupported causes as null
The prompt grounds claims in evidence_ids and defines human-review behavior
The evaluation plan compares the same representative and adversarial cases and tracks schema validity, unsupported-claim rate, latency, and token usage

evals.prompt: Polish this prompt specifically for Google Stitch so it generates a responsive fintech landing page with a dark visual system: 'make me a modern bank website'.
evals.expected_output: The new-prompt skill stays out of scope and routes the request to an installed Stitch-focused skill when available.
expectations: The request is identified as Stitch-specific rather than handled as a general LLM prompt
The response directs the task to an available Stitch-focused skill without claiming this package includes one or duplicating its UI-specific workflow
